info.title: Platehouse API
info.description:
The Platehouse public API, for scripts and tools such as AI coding assistants: upload files, search the library, read models, files, plates and their print estimates, and add or remove tags and collection memberships.

It never deletes, trashes or purges anything, and a model in the trash is invisible to it.

Every request needs an API token, made in Settings, sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Cookies are ignored, and no answer carries CORS headers, so a web page on another site cannot call it.

Errors answer JSON with an error code word and, often, a message sentence, except the tus upload operations, which answer plain text, and a 414 (a path too long), which uses the server's own shape. JSON bodies are at most 1 MiB; uploads are at most 536870912 bytes (512 MiB). The guide is docs/api.md in the Platehouse repository.

bearer.description: An API token, made in Settings > API tokens and shown once. It starts with ph_. Send it on every request as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Revoking it in Settings stops it at once and leaves other tokens working.

get.description:
Live models, best match first and then by name, a page at a time. With no parameters it lists the whole library. q, tag, collection and creator can be combined, and each narrows the list. Models in the trash never appear.

To read every page, pass the answer's nextCursor as cursor until nextCursor is null. Keep the other parameters the same from page to page.

externalRef is a lookup rather than a filter: it answers the one live model with that reference, or none, and cannot be sent with any other parameter.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Words matched in name, caption, creator and tags, ignoring case

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Only models with this tag, ignoring case

parameters.name: collection
parameters.description: Only models in this collection, ignoring case

parameters.name: creator
parameters.description: Only models by this creator, exactly as written

parameters.name: externalRef
parameters.description: The live model with this reference (zero or one); cannot be combined with the others

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: nextCursor from the previous page, to read the next one

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Models per page, 1 to 200; 50 when left out

schema.description: One page of models

license.description: Usually an SPDX licence id, such as CC-BY-4.0; any string is accepted

licenseNote.description: Licence text that is not an SPDX id

externalRef.description: Where the model came from, such as manyfold:<id>; unique

collections.description: The collections it is in, A to Z

nextCursor.description: Pass as cursor for the next page; null on the last page

models.name: Cable clip
models.caption: A snap-on clip for desk cables
models.description: Prints without supports. Use PETG for a stronger snap.
models.creator: Example Maker

post.summary: Make a model with no files yet
post.description:
Makes an empty model with the details given, ready for files: upload them with its id as modelId in the upload's metadata. Only name is required. Tags and collections are made on first use. A field this API does not know is refused rather than ignored. The name given is kept: a .3mf uploaded into the model later never renames it from its title, though its MakerWorld details fill any of caption, creator, description and licence the model left empty.

externalRef records where a model came from and is unique, so an import that runs twice makes each model once: a taken externalRef is 409, with trashed saying whether that model is in the trash.

get.description:
The file's bytes, exactly as uploaded. Content-Disposition names the file (with its real extension, such as .3mf) and Content-Length is its size. HEAD answers the same headers with no body, after checking the bytes are in storage. A file of a model in the trash is 404.

An interrupted download can be resumed with a Range header: one byte range per request, answered 206 with that part. Several ranges in one Range header are answered 200 with the whole file. If-Range takes the ETag only, not a date, and the range is used only while the file's bytes are unchanged. A range that starts at or past the end of the file is 416. HEAD ignores Range.

This is the scripted download. The Open in Bambu Studio and Open in OrcaSlicer buttons on a model page use short-lived slicer links instead, made by the web app for a signed-in person; a token cannot make one.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The file's id

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: One byte range, such as bytes=0-1048575. Multi-range is answered 200 in full.

parameters.name: if-range
parameters.description: The ETag from an earlier answer. The range is used only while the file's bytes are unchanged; otherwise the answer is 200 in full.

200.description: The file. Content-Type is the file's own (model/3mf, model/stl, model/step, or text/plain; charset=utf-8 for .scad).

ETag.description: The file's current bytes, as a strong tag for If-Range

206.description: Part of the file, for a Range request.

ETag.description: The file's current bytes, as a strong tag for If-Range

head.description:
The same status and headers as the GET, with no body. The file's bytes, exactly as uploaded. Content-Disposition names the file (with its real extension, such as .3mf) and Content-Length is its size. HEAD answers the same headers with no body, after checking the bytes are in storage. A file of a model in the trash is 404.

An interrupted download can be resumed with a Range header: one byte range per request, answered 206 with that part. Several ranges in one Range header are answered 200 with the whole file. If-Range takes the ETag only, not a date, and the range is used only while the file's bytes are unchanged. A range that starts at or past the end of the file is 416. HEAD ignores Range.

This is the scripted download. The Open in Bambu Studio and Open in OrcaSlicer buttons on a model page use short-lived slicer links instead, made by the web app for a signed-in person; a token cannot make one.

post.description:
Creates a resumable upload of a known size (tus 1.0.0 creation). The size goes in Upload-Length, at most 536870912 bytes (512 MiB). Upload-Metadata must carry filename, whose extension says what the file is: .3mf, .stl, .step, .stp or .scad. Add modelId to put the file into an existing model, or batch (and combine) to group several uploads; with neither, the file becomes a model of its own, named from the .3mf's MakerWorld title when it has one, else from the file's name.

duplicates says what happens when a live model already holds a file with the same SHA-256: allow (the default) stores it anyway and the result lists the copies; skip stores nothing and the result is failed with code duplicate. A file in the trash never counts.

The answer's Location is the upload's address. Send the bytes there with PATCH, then poll GET /uploads/{id}/result until it says done or failed. The body of this request may already carry the first bytes, or the whole file, when it is sent with Content-Type: application/offset+octet-stream (tus creation-with-upload).

Nothing is stored until the last byte arrives. An unfinished upload is deleted 24 hours after it was created, whatever has arrived by then, or after an hour when it has received no byte. One token may hold at most 20 unfinished uploads at once.

parameters.description: The tus protocol version; always 1.0.0

parameters.description: The file's size in bytes, at most 536870912

parameters.description: tus Upload-Metadata: comma-separated pairs, each a key, a space and the value in base64. filename is required. modelId adds the file to that live model. batch (1 to 200 characters) groups the uploads that share it; with combine 1 or true they become one model, with combine 0, false or left out each is its own model. modelId cannot be sent with batch or combine. duplicates is skip or allow, allow when left out. Other keys are ignored.

head.description: Upload-Offset says how many bytes have arrived; send the rest with PATCH from there. Use it after a cut-off, such as a network change. Once the file has been imported, Upload-Offset equals Upload-Length, so nothing is sent again. If the import failed with nothing saved, the answer is 410, and GET /uploads/{id}/result says why. An upload removed by the hourly sweep (an unfinished one 24 hours after it was created, whatever had arrived, or after an hour with no byte; any upload after 24 hours untouched; a finished one 24 hours after its import), or because its import could not be queued, is 404.

patch.description:
Appends the request body to the upload at Upload-Offset, which must equal the bytes received so far (0 for the first request). One PATCH may carry the whole file, as curl does, or the file may be sent in chunks of any size, each starting where the last ended. After a cut-off, ask HEAD /uploads/{id} for the offset and carry on.

When the last byte lands, the file is queued for import; read GET /uploads/{id}/result for the outcome. A single request may take up to about 72 minutes, enough to send 512 MiB at 1 Mbit/s.
